headline: Choose whether to extend or restart
statement: Return the largest sum of any nonempty contiguous subarray of nums.
intuition: The best subarray ending at the next value has only two possibilities: extend the previous best ending sum, or start at this value. A negative previous sum makes extending worse than starting fresh at the new value. Keep both the best ending here and the best seen anywhere.
approach: Initialize ending and best to the first value.
At each later value, compare starting fresh with extending ending.
Update the global best and return it.
correctness: Every subarray ending at i either starts at i or extends a subarray ending at i-1. Choosing the better option gives the optimal ending sum by induction. Taking the maximum over all ending positions therefore covers every nonempty subarray.
bruteForce: Enumerate every start/end pair and accumulate sums in O(n²) time.

complexity.explanation: Only two running sums are needed.

pitfalls: Initialize from the first element, not zero: all-negative arrays have a negative answer.
Return the global best rather than the final ending sum.
